title: Two Overlooked Skills Predict Children's Reading Success
paragraphs: Why do some children find reading hard? A team at Texas A&M University looked for the answer. They gathered data from 137 different tests and combined about 50,000 results.

The team found two skills that predict reading best. The first is auditory processing, which means hearing and separating the sounds in spoken words. The second is knowing many words and having a lot of general knowledge.

General intelligence also helped, but less than older studies said. Seeing and visual skills did not matter much for reading. The scientist who led the work says that reading problems do not mean a child has low ability.

questions.q: How many tests did the team use?

questions.a: Hearing and separating the sounds in spoken words.

questions.q: Did visual skills matter much for reading?
questions.a: No, they did not matter much.
